title: the Coral Triangle Rising
premise: Ansel Montrose, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Coral Triangle's most dangerous optimists, follows a freak low tide into a sea cave that legends say grants safe passage across the mountains — for a price. The cave's tide-marks rewrite themselves around whoever enters, and Ansel discovers it trades in memory: every mile of passage costs him a piece of his past. Racing the early snows alongside a disgraced cartographer and a girl who claims the cave as her birthright, he must decide what version of himself is worth surviving as. In the end, Ansel pays with the memory of why he owed the debt at all, walks out free on the far side, and chooses to rebuild — not by recovering what he lost, but by belonging to the people who crossed with him.
about_author: Yara Sandoval is a former marine surveyor who spent six years charting tidal caves across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose pasts are heavier than their packs.

chapters.title: The Debt Collectors Wear Smiles
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Chasing a storm off the Coral Triangle coast to earn salvage money, Ansel instead loses his rig and faces Veyra Solenne, the cheerful moneylender whose optimism is more frightening than any threat. She gives him one week. The emotional beat is cornered desperation masked with bravado.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A once-in-a-lifetime ebb exposes a cave mouth locals refuse to name. Inside, tide-marks glow and rearrange, and a voice offers passage over the mountains — ahead of schedule, ahead of the snows. Ansel steps in. The beat is reckless hope overriding caution.

chapters.title: The First Payment
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Mid-passage, the cave takes its toll: his mother's face dissolves from memory. He stumbles out onto the mountain trail disoriented, where he meets Odile Ferran, a cartographer expelled from her guild for mapping this very route. The beat is grief without knowing what was grieved.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Owns the Mountain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They encounter Kess, a teenage guide who claims ancestral right to the cave and demands to come along — or report them. Her knowledge of the tide-marks proves real. The beat is wary alliance; three strangers bound by necessity rather than trust.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. The weather turns weeks early. Kess reveals the cave has passages that only open in storms, forcing them to climb higher into danger. Ansel pays again — losing the memory of his sister. The beat is mounting dread as survival begins costing identity itself.

chapters.title: Odile's Map of Missing Things
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confesses she was exiled because her maps showed the cave's memory-price, and the guild profited from hiding it. She's been searching for someone who entered and returned whole. There hasn't been one. The beat is bitter revelation and deepening stakes.

chapters.title: Veyra at the Pass
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Impossible but true: Veyra Solenne waits at the high pass — the cave's debt and hers are entangled, and she means to collect both. She offers Ansel a deal: betray Kess's claim to the cave, and his debts vanish. The beat is temptation sharpened by exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Storm That Opens Doors
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. The great storm hits. Kess refuses to surrender her birthright; Ansel, remembering nothing of why he ever needed money, turns on Veyra anyway — instinct outrunning memory. The trio flees into the cave's deepest, storm-only passage. The beat is loyalty proven by a man who can't recall earning it.

chapters.title: The Last Tide-Mark
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the cave's heart, the final payment is demanded: everything, all remaining memory, for guaranteed exit. Ansel instead offers the debt itself — the reason he borrowed, the shame that started it. The cave accepts. The beat is sacrifice as self-definition: choosing what to lose.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The three emerge on the far side into clear light, snows behind them. Ansel remembers little but keeps Odile's hand-drawn map and Kess's promise to teach him the tides. Veyra's claim dissolved with the debt. The beat is quiet resolution: a man rebuilt not from his past, but from his companions.
